auth_clean_url: Clean auth URL (paste this in a browser on any device, then bring back the code it gives you): {url}
who_self: This session (yours, the one running this script): {origin}
who_alone: You're alone: {n} session(s), all local and yours ({user}).
who_not_alone: You're NOT alone: {n} active session(s) total.
who_nat_warning: Behind NAT — local IP is {ip} (inbound SSH from outside this network needs port forwarding).
who_hint: Who else is connected: run `{cmd}` to see (doesn't run by default).
note_codex_no_cli_usage: no usage % available via non-interactive CLI
note_antigravity_no_usage: no usage % available (not confirmed via CLI) — run 'agy' once to sign in
note_antigravity_skipped: not checked (pass --check-antigravity to probe; only do this after 'agy' has logged in once — otherwise it opens a Google OAuth browser popup)
note_grok_skipped: not checked (pass --check-grok to probe; opens a real interactive grok session in a throwaway tmux window to read its Usage limit tab, since that data doesn't exist headlessly — see docs/NOTES.md)
note_grok_no_usage: no usage % available — the live tmux probe didn't find the Usage limit tab (grok's session may not have started in time, or its popup layout changed; not necessarily an auth problem)
grok_experimental_caveat: ⚠ experimental — treat this bar as "some signal", not a reliable countdown: confirmed live that a free account got cut off entirely while this same reading still said 0% used, so the number above and whatever actually stops you don't appear to track the same thing
menu_installing_ui: Setting up the interactive picker (one-time, installs 'textual' into ~/.selectorai/venv)...
menu_ui_failed: Couldn't set up the interactive picker (offline? no venv module?) — falling back to the plain menu.
launch_codex_safe: Launching Codex in sandboxed automatic mode (--ask-for-approval never --sandbox workspace-write)...
models_caution: Heads up: {providers} may prompt you to log in (opening a browser) while listing models, even if you're already signed in elsewhere.
models_result_static: {label}: {models} (static list from --help text, not a live query)
session_background_on_msg: Background sessions: ON — launches will run inside a reattachable tmux session (survives SSH drops).
session_background_off_msg: Background sessions: OFF — launches run directly, no tmux wrapping.
session_background_hint_on: {cmd} background on    # persist: always wrap launches in a reattachable tmux session (default when tmux is installed)
session_background_hint_off: {cmd} background off   # persist: launch directly, no tmux wrapping
session_no_tmux: tmux isn't installed on this machine — background sessions are unavailable until it is, regardless of this setting.
setup_needs_tty: Guided setup needs an interactive terminal — stdin and stdout must both be a real tty. Run `{cmd}` directly (not through a pipe), or add --dry-run to preview the whole flow non-interactively.
setup_dry_run_banner: Dry run: nothing will be installed, signed into, or changed — every step below just prints what it WOULD do.
setup_would_language: (dry-run) Would offer the language picker here.
setup_install_hint: Tip: `{cmd}` updates everything already installed, any time.
setup_auth_no_status_check: No non-interactive way to check {label}'s sign-in status.
setup_antigravity_not_installed: Antigravity isn't installed — nothing to check.
setup_antigravity_caveat: Checking Antigravity's real quota runs `agy -p "/usage"`, which can pop up a real Google sign-in browser window if the session isn't fresh — and Antigravity's own session handling is known to be flaky (antigravity-cli#57/#18), so this can happen even right after a previous successful login.
setup_confirm_antigravity_on: Turn this check ON by default? [y/N]
setup_would_antigravity_on: (dry-run) Would offer to turn this check on.
setup_antigravity_hint: Leaving it off for now — turn it on any time with `{cmd}`.
setup_grok_check_not_installed: Grok Build isn't installed — nothing to check.
setup_grok_check_caveat: Checking Grok's real quota opens a real interactive `grok` session inside a throwaway tmux window and reads its Usage limit tab — there's no headless equivalent (confirmed: `grok -p "/status" --output-format json` never includes it). This takes several seconds every time (cold start can be ~15-20s) and depends on grok's current TUI layout, unlike the other providers' checks.
setup_confirm_grok_check_on: Turn this check ON by default? [y/N]
setup_would_grok_check_on: (dry-run) Would offer to turn this check on.
setup_grok_check_hint: Leaving it off for now — turn it on any time with `{cmd}`.
setup_tmux_available: tmux is available — launches run inside a reattachable background session by default. Disable with `{cmd}`.
setup_tmux_missing: tmux isn't installed, so background sessions stay dormant until it is. Hint: sudo apt install tmux
setup_would_theme: (dry-run) Would offer the theme picker here.
setup_would_models: (dry-run) Would offer to refresh model listings.
setup_would_finish: (dry-run) Would force-refresh every provider's status and print it here.
setup_closing: Setup done. Run `{cmd}` any time to start.
